backend_limitations.note: Parity requirements describing current behavior, not promises to implement missing codegen. Derived from source.

items.behavior: Past -fsyntax-only / -E, only x86_64 ELF targets are accepted; anything else is fatal: 'unsupported target {arch}-{os}-{abi}, currently only x86-64 elf is supported'.
-O0 selects the non-optimizing assembly backend (use_assembly_backend); every other -O level goes through IR (tree.genIr) and Ir.render.
Only x86_64 is implemented; any other arch panics 'genAsm not implemented'.

Emits data only. Function definitions fail with diagnostic 'TODO: Codegen functions'. Aggregate/array/struct/union initializers -> 'TODO: Codegen multiple inits' / 'Codegen aggregates'; _Complex -> 'TODO: Codegen _Complex values'; non-8/16/32/64/128-bit ints -> 'TODO: Codegen _BitInt values'; pointers -> 'TODO: Codegen pointer'. Scalars, floats (16/32/64/80/128), strings, .bss/.data/.tdata/.tbss/.comm, -fdata-sections, and the .note.GNU-stack section are emitted.
Every IR decl fails with 'TODO implement lowering functions'; Driver reports 'unable to render Ir to machine code: ...'. So no object code is produced for any function via the IR path.

Fails with 'TODO ...' for: global assembly, struct bitfields, union types, blocks, complex, atomic, VLAs, nullptr_t, case ranges, several statements/expressions/casts/lvalues/builtins/initializers, static/thread_local compound literals, memcpy, and global variables (genVar).
Only ELF object format exists (other formats are unreachable).
